feature.name: Preview Production Data Toggle on Stats Page
feature.description: A UI toggle on /stats.html and /stats-games.html lets admins on dev.play.carkedit.com or staging.play.carkedit.com flip data fetching from local to live production data. Persists as ?source=prod, shows a red banner while active, hides mutation buttons (DEV toggles, base-cost edits), and is hidden entirely on play.carkedit.com itself.

screenshots.description: Pre-auth dashboard state on localhost — proves the modified renderPage / readSourceFromUrl / bootDashboard paths boot cleanly. The toggle button itself appears in the header after sign-in; needs the real dev deploy to be captured in-flow.

commits: feat: add 'preview production data' toggle to stats page (#251)
docs: explain why /api/carkedit needs no CORS middleware (carkedit-api #124)
framing: The story isn't really the toggle — it's the surprise mid-build. The original plan added a /api/carkedit/* CORS middleware to the Express stack so the dev/staging page could fetch prod data cross-origin. While verifying with curl I noticed the response already had Access-Control-Allow-Origin reflected back, and tracing it found the colyseus framework (which the API uses for the realtime card game) attaches its own permissive CORS handler at the HTTP server level via server.prependListener('request', ...). It reflects any Origin, allows credentials, and answers OPTIONS preflight before our Express stack ever runs. So my planned ~25-line middleware would have been dead code — colyseus had already written the headers and stolen the OPTIONS response. The 'fix' became a 9-line comment block in src/index.ts explaining this to future readers so nobody else burns a session re-discovering it. Net for the user: a 'two-repo feature' became a 'one-repo feature plus documentation,' and the only meaningful code lives client-side: a getProdFirebaseConfig() helper that pins authDomain to play.carkedit.com so the OAuth popup runs through prod's same-origin /__/auth/* reverse-proxy (the same Safari ITP workaround already used for the primary Firebase init), a dynamic apiBase() helper that flips between '' and 'https://play.carkedit.com', and a secondary Firebase app for prod auth. The boot ordering is the subtle bit: checkAdminAndBoot must verify the local admin first, so a ?source=prod URL is captured into pendingDataSource and only applied after the local dashboard renders — otherwise the page would try to use a prod token that doesn't exist yet. The wider takeaway: verify your assumptions on a running server before writing the code your plan calls for. The cheapest curl test would have caught this on day one of planning, not at Gate 2.

feature.name: In-flight deploy badge on /deploy dashboard
feature.description: When a tier reports an in-flight deploy via /versions (phase ∈ {starting, running}), the affected version cell now renders a 'deploying…' or 'starting…' text chip next to the pulsing ⚠ icon. The Deployed versions table also auto-refetches every 5s while any tier is in-flight, then stops cleanly when all tiers reach a terminal phase.

screenshots.description: All three tiers (Live / Staging / Dev) show the api cell with a pulsing ⚠ icon and a muted-yellow 'deploying…' chip. Other columns (client, deploy) stay ✓ — the badge is per-cell, not per-row.
Starting-phase variant: the client column shows ⚠ + a 'starting…' chip while the api and deploy columns stay clean. Same visual, distinct text — the phase comes straight from the /versions response.

commits: feat: in-flight deploy badge + tighter /versions polling (#70)
framing: The icon already pulsed yellow when a deploy was in flight, but the change was easy to miss from across the room — and worse, /versions wasn't being re-fetched, so the dashboard stayed stale for 30-60s after a push-to-main even though the cache TTL alone wasn't the bottleneck. Two small fixes, one concept: make the in-flight state legible. A text chip ('deploying…' / 'starting…') sits next to the pulsing icon so the state reads from peripheral vision, and a self-rearming setTimeout chain re-fetches /versions every 5s while any tier is in-flight, then stops cleanly. The chip is gated on envBody.current.target === col, so the existing requiredApiVersion-mismatch warn case (which is also ⚠) stays badge-less — pickIcon now returns inFlightPhase to disambiguate the two paths. JS/CSS only, no server contract change, no deployment impact. Verified end-to-end with Playwright MCP by stubbing the /versions response: badge appears within 1s of an in-flight phase entering the payload, polling runs at the expected 5s cadence (15 calls / 26.5s / 3 envs), and polling stops completely within one cycle of returning to current=null.

feature.name: Promote build panel — Tag for staging / Tag for production
feature.description: Two env-aware buttons on the /deploy admin page that create vs<version> / v<version> tags on all 3 carkedit repos in one click — promoting a build from dev → staging → production. Each button is enabled only on its source environment, with a tooltip naming the required env on the disabled side. Server-side ENV_TIER enforcement matches the client-side gating.

screenshots.description: Dev tier — Tag for staging (vs…) enabled (purple), Tag for production (v…) greyed out with tooltip Only available on the staging server (current: dev). Panel sits between the Tags card and the deploy form.
Staging tier — inverse: Tag for production (v…) enabled, Tag for staging (vs…) greyed out with tooltip Only available on the dev server (current: staging). Same panel, env-driven role swap.
Prod tier — both buttons greyed out with their respective tooltips. The promotion workflow is read-only from prod so visibility is preserved without action.

commits: feat: add Promote build panel — Tag for staging / Tag for production buttons (#59)
framing: Before this, promoting a build from dev to staging meant SSHing into a box and running git tag && git push origin <tag> three times — once per repo — and prod was the same dance again. Nothing stopped you from tagging the wrong env from the wrong machine. The new panel collapses that into one click on the right server, and makes the wrong-server case visually impossible: both buttons render everywhere, but only the contextually-correct one is clickable, with a tooltip explaining why on the disabled side. Backend enforcement (POST /api/admin/deploy/tag returns 403 env_mismatch if ENV_TIER doesn't match the requested tag kind) means the disabled UI is purely UX — the server is the trust boundary. Lands on top of PR #62's requiredApiVersion infrastructure: tags created here are pure promotion markers, and the version-coupling contract (what API version a client tag was built against) lives in package.json where each repo tracks its own. When a vs<version> client tag I just created is later deployed to staging, the chained-deploy code from #62 reads its package.json and auto-deploys the matching API first if needed. The split keeps each piece simple — the tag is a marker, the repo owns the version.

feature.name: Repositioned Current status panel on /deploy + compress + auto-reload on success
feature.description: On the deploy admin UI, the Current status panel now lives directly under Deployed versions by default — paired visually with the version table it describes. When you press Deploy, the panel relocates to sit immediately above the form so the live progress sits right next to the button you just clicked. On a successful deploy the per-step exit-code list collapses (single green confirmation line), and 1.5s later the page auto-reloads so deployed-versions, Recent activity, and Tags all repaint with the new state. Failure / skipped deploys deliberately don't reload — the user needs to read the error.

Immediately after pressing Deploy: the Current status panel has relocated to sit directly above the form. Same DOM section — moved via insertBefore — so your eye doesn't have to leave the button you just clicked.

Success state, compressed: the green dot + 'Succeeded:' line is all that remains. The step list disappears via a CSS rule keyed on data-phase="success". The page reloads 1.5s after this state appears.

commits: feat: reposition Current status panel + compress on success + reload after success (#60)
version: bump to v0.14.0000 (post-merge MINOR)
framing: Tiny UX paper-cut that became a habit: press Deploy, scroll down to see what's happening, scroll back up to read the new version. Three small changes fix the whole loop. (1) Status lives next to the versions table by default so 'is this server healthy?' and 'what's it running?' read together. (2) When you actually press Deploy, the panel jumps to where your eye already is — right above the button. (3) On success the panel collapses to a single line and the page reloads, so the versions/activity/tags repaint with the new state automatically. Implementation is small (41 insertions, 14 deletions, 5 files) but each piece exists for a specific reason; failure and skip cases explicitly DON'T reload so the user can read the error. Both the main form and the inline branch-chip Deploy buttons get the same behaviour because both code paths share triggerDeploy().

feature.name: Wildcard Eulogy BYE Cards
feature.description: Added 2× Wildcard Eulogy entries to the BYE card deck, bringing the total to 68 cards to match the physical print file. The Wildcard Eulogy is a special end-of-game card where players earn bonus points by giving each other eulogies.

commits: feat: add Wildcard Eulogy cards to BYE deck (68 total)
framing: The BYE deck digital data now faithfully matches the physical card print file. The Wildcard Eulogy is one of the most fun cards in the game — players save it until the end and then roast each other with eulogies for bonus points. Having it correctly represented (twice, as in the physical deck) ensures the online version delivers the same end-game energy.

feature.name: Full-Screen Card on Card Test Page
feature.description: The card on card-test.html now scales to fill the entire viewport — height or width, whichever is reached first — while maintaining the 5:7 aspect ratio. The main UI (title, deck switcher, card, nav arrows) is locked to 100vh so nothing scrolls off screen; the JSON inspector remains accessible by scrolling below.

commits: feat: scale card to fill viewport on card test page
framing: The card test page previously showed cards at a tiny 160px fixed width — basically a thumbnail. Now it actually fills the screen, making it useful for reviewing artwork, checking typography legibility, and demoing card designs at the scale players will see them in the game.

feature.name: Dev Dashboard
feature.description: Internal development dashboard with contribution graph (all 5 repos), multi-repo commit history, mini card tester, color palette viewer, wiki updates, todo board, rate limit display, and localStorage caching for resilience when rate-limited.

commits: fix: dashboard iteration 3 - rate limit display, localStorage cache, UX fixes
framing: The dev dashboard gives the team a single page to monitor all project activity across 5 repos, test card rendering, review the color system, and track wiki/todo progress — without leaving the browser. The rate limit display and localStorage cache solve a real pain point: GitHub's 60 req/hr unauthenticated limit was silently breaking the dashboard during testing, now it gracefully degrades with cached data.

feature.name: Remove Player from Lobby
feature.description: Tapping a player chip in the Lobby now reveals a red ✕ button. Tapping ✕ removes that player from the game. Tapping the same chip again dismisses the button without removing — a safe two-step interaction that's lobby-only and invisible during gameplay.

commits: feat: tap player chip in lobby to reveal remove button
framing: Before this change there was no way to undo adding a player — you'd have to reload the whole page. Now it's a quick tap-tap to correct a typo or remove someone who sat down at the wrong table. Small UX detail, big reduction in friction at game setup time.

feature.name: Auto-populate Random Player Name in Lobby
feature.description: When the Add button is clicked with an empty name field in the lobby, a random name is auto-selected from a dev placeholder pool (Brennan, Simon, Leonie, Danikah, Lowe, Hatton, Sanderson) — skipping any already in use, and doing nothing gracefully when the pool is exhausted.

commits: feat: auto-populate random player name when lobby input is empty
framing: Setting up a test game used to require typing every player name manually — a small but annoying friction point during playtesting. Now you can spam Add and the game fills in the squad for you. It's a dev convenience feature flagged for replacement before launch, but it makes iterating on lobby flow and game mechanics dramatically faster.

feature.name: Phase 2/3 Turn-Based Gameplay (LIVE & BYE)
feature.description: Implements the core scoring gameplay loop for Phase 2 (LIVE) and Phase 3 (BYE). Players take turns as 'The Living Dead' while others pitch cards from their hand. The Living Dead picks their favourite, awarding the winner +1 point. Each player is Living Dead twice per phase (2 full rounds). Both phases share a single manager with different decks.

commits: feat: implement Phase 2/3 (LIVE & BYE) turn-based gameplay
fix: show Living Dead's die card instead of random LIVE card as prompt
merge: incorporate main branch changes (player removal, random names, backgrounds)
refactor: use card.js component for all card rendering in Phase 2/3
framing: This is the biggest feature drop yet — Phase 2/3 is the actual game. Phase 1 was just drawing a death card, but Phase 2 is where players strategise, pitch, persuade, and compete for points. The pass-the-phone UX makes it work on a single device (no server needed), the Living Dead skull icon adds personality, and the card inspection overlay lets players really read and appreciate each card before playing it. The shared manager architecture means Phase 3 (BYE) came essentially free — same code, different deck. All cards now render through the shared card.js component with full illustrations, matching the physical card game's visual richness.

feature.name: Dynamic Card Spacing in Hand Fan
feature.description: Cards in the Phase 2 hand fan now spread evenly across the full width of the container using CSS calc() percentage-based positioning, replacing fixed 43px pixel offsets. Works at any screen width and handles any number of cards.

commits: fix: dynamic percentage-based card positioning in hand fan
framing: The hand fan was using a hardcoded 43px offset between cards — fine on one screen size but cramped or misaligned on others. Now the formula is calc((100% - 135px) * index / (count - 1)), so the first card sits flush left, the last card sits flush right, and everything in between divides the space perfectly. It's a small detail that makes the game feel polished across all device widths.

feature.name: Hand Overlay Navigation Arrows + Selected Card Protrusion
feature.description: Added ‹ › navigation arrows to the card inspect overlay so players can browse their entire hand without closing it. The currently-viewed card also protrudes ~35% of its height above the hand fan as a visual indicator of which card is selected.

screenshots.description: Inspect overlay with ‹ › navigation arrows flanking the card
Selected card protruding above the hand fan into the gameboard, other cards visible below

commits: feat: add hand overlay navigation arrows and selected card protrusion
merge: resolve conflict with main responsive hand layout
framing: Before this, players had to close the overlay to see a different card — tedious when you're trying to weigh up your options under social pressure. Now you can swipe through your whole hand in one tap each. The protruding card is a small but satisfying detail: you can glance down at the hand and immediately see which card you're currently inspecting, even with the overlay open. Both features together make card selection feel fluid rather than clunky.

feature.name: Card Grid Component
feature.description: New reusable card-grid component renders submitted cards in a clean 2-column grid. Used on the revealed screen (cards appear in a grid instead of overlapping scatter, die/prompt card hidden) and the judging screen (Living Dead picks their favourite from tappable cards with hover highlights). Old bespoke CSS removed.

commits: feat: add card-grid component and use for revealed/judging screens
framing: The old revealed screen piled all submitted cards on top of each other in a random scatter — confusing and hard to read under the social pressure of the reveal moment. Now they lay out in a clean 2-column grid so every card is fully visible at the same time. The same grid is reused on the judging screen where the Living Dead taps their favourite, making the interaction clear and consistent. Standardising this into a shared component means any future screen that needs a card selection grid — like a scoreboard or highlight reel — can use it in one line.

feature.name: Card Preview Overlay on Judging Screen
feature.description: When a judge clicks a submitted card during Phase 2/3 judging, it now opens the same full-screen inspect overlay used when picking from hand — large card, deck-coloured nav arrows (green for LIVE), and a "Pick This Card" confirm button. Nav arrows let you browse all submitted cards before committing. Backdrop tap dismisses without selecting.

commits: feat: add card preview overlay to judging screen
framing: Before this change, tapping a card on the judging screen immediately picked a winner — no chance to zoom in, re-read the card, or build suspense. Now the Living Dead can tap through all submitted cards one by one in a full-screen overlay before committing. The same overlay code that powers hand selection was extracted into a shared renderInspectOverlay() component, so the judging preview inherits all the same polish: big card, deck-coloured arrows, and a satisfying confirm button. Zero code duplication, consistent UX across both contexts.

feature.name: Birthday Picker
feature.description: Players can now have a birthday (month + day) stored alongside their name, entered via two dropdowns during lobby setup. The birthday appears with a 🎂 icon contextually: always in the Lobby, on your active turn in Phase 1, and next to the Living Dead player in Phase 2/3/4. Score is shown at all other times. The dev player pool is pre-populated with birthdates for instant testing.

commits: feat: add birthday picker and display to player list
framing: Carked It is a social game played around a table — everyone knows each other. Adding birthdates gives the game a personal touch: your birthday shows up when it's your turn in Phase 1, and when you're The Living Dead judging everyone's cards. It's a small detail that makes the digital version feel warmer and more personal than a generic party game app.

feature.name: Hand Footer Buttons
feature.description: All action buttons in the hand area (Flip Card, Done Dying, Start Round, Reveal Cards, Start Pitching, Done Pitching, Redraw Hand) now render inside a unified .hand__footer subsection with a consistent white background — visually part of the hand UI panel rather than floating separately on the dark game screen.

commits: refactor: unify hand action buttons into consistent .hand__footer section
style: remove border-top from .hand__footer
framing: Seven different action buttons across Phase 1, 2, and 3 were being rendered through three completely different patterns — a manual hand div in Phase 1, a bare footer prop in Phase 2/3 selecting, and a separate .phase-actions div floating outside the hand component entirely. The inconsistency was invisible to players but a maintenance headache in code. Now every hand-area button goes through the same .hand__footer slot, appears on the same white background, and is positioned identically regardless of which phase you're in. It's the kind of refactor that makes the codebase feel coherent — the UI now expresses a clear intent rather than accumulating workarounds.

feature.name: CarkedIt Favicon
feature.description: The browser tab, Apple home screen icon, Android shortcut, and Windows tile now all show the CarkedIt card front image — the same favicon used on carkedit.com. Four PNG sizes (32×32, 180×180, 192×192, 270×270) are self-hosted in assets/ and declared via standard link tags in index.html.

commits: feat: add CarkedIt favicon matching carkedit.com branding
framing: Before this, CarkedIt Online had no favicon — the browser tab showed a blank page icon. Now it shows the same iconic card-front image as carkedit.com, giving the game a consistent brand identity across the browser tab, home screen shortcuts, and pinned tiles. It's a small detail but a meaningful one: it signals polish and makes the game feel like a real product when players bookmark it or add it to their phone's home screen.

feature.name: Hide Create Room on Join Links

framing: A small but important UX fix for the share-a-link flow. When you text a friend a join link, they should land on a focused screen that says "enter your name and hit Join" — not a screen that also offers to create a whole new room. Removing the distraction makes the join-via-link experience feel intentional and polished.

feature.name: Lobby Pack Filter Tabs
feature.description: The host pack selector in the online lobby now has 4 filter tabs with white SVG icons: Official Decks (skull), My Decks (person), Public Decks (globe), and My Favourites (heart). Each pack also gets a heart toggle for favouriting. Backed by a new is_official admin flag and a full favourites system (DB table, endpoints, viewer-aware listings). Admins get a 'Mark as Official Deck' checkbox in the card designer.

screenshots.description: All four filter tabs (skull/person/globe/heart) rendered across the four states with active-tab purple underline, totals row, and per-pack heart toggles

feat: lobby pack filter tabs (Official / My / Public / Favourites)

framing: The expansion pack list was about to get unwieldy as more user-created and public decks ship. Filter tabs scope it down so the host can find what they want fast — official curated decks for a quick standard game, their own drafts to test, the community's published packs to discover, or their saved favourites for quick replays. The favourites system is brand new (no DB table existed) and is the lever that makes 'I liked that deck last week' a one-tap action instead of a search. The admin 'Mark as Official' flag means the team can curate which community packs get the green-tick treatment without code changes. Small UI feature, big infrastructure under the hood.

feature.name: Mark Games / NPS / Decks as Dev from Dashboard
feature.description: Added clickable DEV toggle buttons on game rows, NPS survey responses, and expansion pack rows in the admin dashboard. Each toggle shows a themed in-page HTML/CSS confirmation modal (no browser popup), then calls an admin PATCH endpoint. The packs PATCH endpoint already existed; new endpoints PATCH /api/carkedit/games/:id/dev and PATCH /api/carkedit/surveys/:id/dev were added in carkedit-api.

commits: feat(dashboard): toggle is_dev on games, NPS responses, and packs
feat(dashboard): add PATCH endpoints to toggle is_dev on games and surveys
framing: Until now, marking a record as a dev/test entry could only happen at creation time, and only packs could be flipped after the fact. Real playtest sessions inevitably mix in throwaway games and dummy NPS responses that pollute the live stats. With one-click dashboard toggles and the existing With Dev / No Dev / Only Dev filters, the team can now triage that noise after the fact instead of having to remember to flag things up front. The in-page confirmation modal (replacing the default browser popup) is a small detail that keeps the dashboard feeling cohesive and on-brand, and the same PATCH endpoint shape is used for all three entity types so the client code is symmetric.

feature.name: Swipe and Drag Navigation for Card Lists and Previews
feature.description: Added natural swipe and drag gestures across every horizontal card list, pack list, player list, and full-screen card preview in the client — with zero changes to any existing overlay or card-list call site.

commits: feat(touch): swipe navigation for card lists and inspect overlays
feat(touch): drag-to-scroll for horizontal card and list strips
feat(touch): disable native drag + context menu on card images
framing: Before this PR, card strips on mobile were only navigable with tiny arrow buttons, and on desktop you couldn't pan them at all — you were stuck clicking the arrows. Worse, clicking a card image would start the native browser image-drag instead of scrolling the list. This feature turns every horizontal list into a natural swipe-flick surface on touch and a click-and-drag pan on desktop, with scroll-snap landing the strip on a card boundary after release. The inspect overlay (hand, judging, pack detail, dashboard preview) also gets swipe-to-navigate between prev/next cards. The design principle is worth noting: every surface — hand inspect, judging overlay, dashboard preview, lobby pack preview, marketplace pack detail, edit pack, player list chips, dashboard analytics — inherits the new behaviour through two document-level pointer delegates and a structural overflow-x test, with zero changes to the eight-plus call sites that render these lists. One DRY shared primitive, automatic coverage of future surfaces. We also hardened card images against right-click-save and native drag, which felt right as part of the same pass since both are about making cards feel like cards, not web images.

feature.name: GitHub Actions Deploy Workflow Migration
feature.description: Rewrote all six GitHub Actions deploy workflows across carkedit-api and carkedit-online to call the new unified carkedit-deploy service via Bearer-authenticated POST endpoints, replacing the legacy PHP webhooks. Renamed deploy-dev.yml to deploy.yml in both repos, kept distinct tag prefixes (vs* for staging, v[0-9]* for prod) to prevent dual-fire, and split secrets per env-target combination.

commits: chore: migrate deploy workflows to carkedit-deploy (Session E)
framing: This is Session E of an eight-session infrastructure migration replacing brittle per-script PHP deploy webhooks with one unified Node service (carkedit-deploy). The workflow rewrite is what makes the new service actually usable from CI — every push to carkedit-api or carkedit-online now flows through the same Bearer-authenticated endpoint, with per-env tokens. Six identical YAML shapes replace six divergent ones. The story arc behind this work is treating deploys like a real piece of software with auth, observability, and audit instead of a pile of one-off shell scripts. The dual-repo squash-merge (not staggered) was the interesting coordination puzzle — both PRs flipped together so the next push can't land in a half-migrated state.

feature.name: Retire Legacy PHP Deploy Webhook
feature.description: Deleted the 246-line carkedit-api/deploy.php — the legacy PHP deploy webhook that used to be hit by CI to git-pull, npm-build, and pm2-reload the API server. The new Node-based carkedit-deploy service has been running cleanly on dev, staging, and prod, and the GitHub Actions workflows (rewritten in Session E) already POST to its Bearer-auth endpoint instead. Two-file diff: deploy.php deleted + package.json version 0.01.0081 → 0.01.0082.

commits: chore: retire legacy deploy.php webhook
framing: This is Session F of the eight-session carkedit-deploy migration — the cleanup pass that finally deletes the legacy PHP from the carkedit-api repo. There is nothing functionally exciting to demo here, and that's exactly the point: a successful infrastructure migration ends with quiet deletions, not fireworks. The new Node service has been running long enough on all three environments that the fallback is no longer earning its keep, and 246 lines of PHP that hand-stitched `sudo -u bitnami bash -c "…"` strings — exactly the shell-escaping minefield the new service was designed to replace — are now gone for good. The carkedit-online side of the same cleanup (Session G) and the server-side script/sudoers tidy-up are scheduled separately. Sometimes the most valuable shipping work in a week is taking dead code out, not putting new code in.

feature.name: Request-level Observability via pino-http
feature.description: Every HTTP request to carkedit-api now emits one structured JSON line to stdout via pino-http — req.id, method, url, statusCode, bytes, responseTime, Firebase uid, and a roomCode field on /api/carkedit/rooms/lookup. Level escalates to warn at >=500ms and error at >=2000ms (LOG_SLOW_WARN_MS / LOG_SLOW_ERROR_MS). X-Request-Id is set on every response and honours inbound values so an upstream load balancer can correlate. Authorization, Cookie, and Set-Cookie headers are redacted; bodies never logged.

commits: feat: add structured per-request logging via pino-http
fix: read content-length from pre-serialized res.headers
framing: A direct follow-up from the 2026-05-08 prod audit. Apache had surfaced three AH01102 errors over four days — one a real ProxyTimeout against /api/carkedit/rooms/lookup, the others Apache losing the connection on /. The API process itself showed no crashes, sane memory, sane load. The working theory was sporadically slow handlers blocking the event loop just long enough to exceed Apache ProxyTimeout. The problem: the API had zero per-request logs. console.error fired when a handler threw, but a slow request that completed normally was invisible to us — and Apache had no idea which handler was responsible. This change adds the missing signal so the next AH01102 event will correlate to a specific log line with method, path, response time, and even a roomCode for the rooms/lookup endpoint. After about 24h of prod data we expect to know which handler is the culprit, and that becomes the input to a follow-up fix-the-slow-handler ticket. The interesting design constraint was log safety: no bodies, no auth headers, no cookies — even though the team uses 10mb image-gen bodies. pino-http handled it with redact paths and a custom res serializer; the unit tests assert no token can leak even if future code accidentally tries to log req.headers. Out of scope on purpose: log shipping (Datadog/CloudWatch), tracing, DB query logging. Each of those is a separate ticket. The principle is: add the cheapest possible visibility first, see what the data reveals, then escalate. Structured stdout JSON is the cheapest possible visibility — pm2 already captures it, jq already parses it, and no infrastructure changed.

feature.name: Per-Environment Firebase Project Separation
feature.description: All three CarkedIt environments (dev / staging / prod) previously shared the single Firebase project carkedit-5cc8e. This change introduces a per-host getFirebaseConfig() selector in carkedit-online so each hostname authenticates against its own Firebase project, and makes carkedit-api's same-origin OAuth proxy derive its target from the service-account JSON's project_id field — so swapping the JSON per environment automatically swaps the proxy too.

commits: feat: per-host Firebase web SDK config
feat: wire real dev + staging Firebase configs
feat: derive Firebase auth proxy target from service-account project_id (carkedit-api #112)
framing: Pre-launch security tightening. Before this, a dev test user was a real prod user, and a misconfigured dev token could authenticate against the prod API. Three separate Firebase projects, treated as fresh — no user migration needed because there are no real prod users yet. The cost of separation scales with active user count, so it's cheap now and gets expensive later. Two interesting things from the build: (1) the brief asserted carkedit-api needed zero code change, but a hardcoded `carkedit-5cc8e.firebaseapp.com` in the Safari ITP same-origin OAuth proxy would have defeated the whole separation — caught during planning. (2) The runbook initially included a 'clone Firestore security rules' step that turned out to be busywork — grep showed the app uses Firebase Auth only, with game data in local SQLite. Lesson: verify assumptions about what a system actually uses before writing the runbook around them.

feature.name: Deploy Versions Table
feature.description: A 3x3 matrix at the top of the deploy admin page (Live/Staging/Dev rows x api/client/deploy columns). Each cell shows the target version that env should be running, with a green check, yellow warn, or red x icon. Hover any icon for the actually-deployed version. The browser fetches data cross-origin from each env in parallel.

screenshots.description: Happy path: all 9 cells populated with real local versions; green checkmarks indicate deployed matches target.
Hover state: CSS tooltip bubble pops above the icon showing the deployed version.
In-progress: a deploy of api is running on all envs; the api column flips to yellow warn icons with a pulsing animation.

commits: feat: deployed-versions table at top of deploy UI fragment
fix: replace native title tooltip with CSS bubble on versions-table icons

feature.name: Highlight current env + link env names in deployment table

version: bump to 0.02.0000 for feature merge
framing: Before this, the deploy admin page was three identical-looking environments on a single screen — easy to lose track of which one you were about to deploy into, with no way to jump to another env except by retyping the host. feature.name: Cross-Env Versions in Deploy Dashboard
feature.description: The Deployed Versions panel on the deploy admin page can now populate rows for all three environments (Live / Staging / Dev), not just the local one. Adds the three carkedit.com origins to the helmet CSP connect-src directive so the browser stops blocking the cross-env fetches.

screenshots.description: Deployed Versions panel populated with real version data from all three envs (Live, Staging, Dev), rendered from the localhost API with the new CSP

commits: fix: allow cross-env fetches in CSP for deploy dashboard
framing: A nice debugging-then-fixing story — what looked like a network failure ("Unreachable: Failed to fetch") turned out to be the page's own CSP blocking the calls. Server CORS was already correct; the browser was refusing to dial out because the helmet allowlist didn't include our own subdomains. One-line whitelist add gets the full deployed-versions panel — across prod, staging, and dev — visible from any env's deploy page. The wider point: it's easy to read "Failed to fetch" as a server problem; CSP is silent unless you're looking at the right console message.

feature.name: Dev Deploys Post to #dev-updates Discord
feature.description: Wired the missing DISCORD_WEBHOOK_DEV env var in carkedit-deploy so dev-tier deploy successes post a 'Dev deploy: <target> @ <ref>' embed to the #dev-updates Discord channel. The Notifier interface and buildDevEmbed branch already existed — only the createNotifier call in src/index.ts wasn't passing webhookDev through, so every dev deploy was silently dropping its embed.

commits: feat: wire DISCORD_WEBHOOK_DEV so dev deploys post to #dev-updates
version: bump to v0.03.0000 (post-merge MINOR)
framing: Three repos already feed merge-event notifications into #dev-updates via a debounced batcher — you can see them in the channel as the daily 'X merges to main, across 3 repos' embed. But the actual dev deploys themselves were invisible: every time a branch pushed and dev redeployed, nothing showed up. Turned out the wiring was 95% in place — Notifier supported a webhookDev slot, discord.ts had a buildDevEmbed for the dev tier, the deploy router was calling notifier.notifyDeploySuccess({ tier: 'dev', ... }) after every successful run — the env var just wasn't being read at boot. Three lines of glue in src/index.ts and the channel now shows both 'merge to main' AND 'deployed to dev' events in one place, which is what the channel description ('Any updates to the dev server get automatically shared here') always promised. Also documented all five DISCORD_WEBHOOK_* env vars in the README — they'd been undocumented since the original webhook PR. The wider lesson: when a feature looks half-shipped, check whether 95% of the plumbing is already there before designing a new system.

feature.name: Deploy Recent Commits Timeline
feature.description: Added a 'Recent commits' panel to the deploy admin page (play.carkedit.com/deploy.html) showing the last 10 commits merged chronologically across carkedit-api, carkedit-online, and carkedit-deploy. Each row shows tag chips and Live/Staging/Dev badges marking which environments currently have that commit deployed. Coordinated commits across repos (paired PRs landing the same change) collapse onto a single row.

screenshots.description: Recent commits panel below the versions table — 10 commits chronologically, with two grouped rows (api+online chips on one row) and yellow tag chips on the rows that own a tag
Same panel with synthetic deployed SHAs — green LIVE / yellow STAGING / blue DEV badges visible on the top two rows where the env's deployed SHA matches

commits: feat: recent-commits timeline panel with Live/Staging/Dev badges (#13)
feat: group coordinated commits + make repo name the commit link
version: bump to v0.04.0000 (post-merge MINOR) (#14)
framing: The deploy admin page already showed which versions were deployed per environment, but operators still had to leave the page and grep GitHub to answer the question they actually have: what's in each version? This panel surfaces that directly — the operator sees 'Live is on this commit, Staging is two commits ahead, Dev's on main HEAD' at a glance. The repo-name-as-link choice (rather than a separate SHA chip) was a direct response to a 'fewer elements per row' design instinct during Gate 2 review; coordinated-commit grouping was the other Gate 2 refinement — twin PRs in carkedit-api and carkedit-online for the same change shouldn't visually occupy two rows of a 10-row list. The endpoint reuses the existing repo-versions GitHub API client pattern (TTL cache, concurrent-fetch coalescing, GITHUB_TOKEN), so no new infrastructure or env-var configuration was needed.

feature.name: Hard-Fail notify-merge + Document the Missing Apache Proxy
feature.description: Three-repo fix for a silent regression: every PR merge in carkedit-online / carkedit-api / carkedit-deploy was firing a notify-merge GitHub Action that POSTed to /api/admin/notify/merge — and every one was getting HTTP 404 because Apache on prod only proxied the sibling /api/admin/deploy/ prefix. The workflow's soft-fail logic (warning + exit 0) had been masking it as green runs for weeks. Three PRs: carkedit-deploy adds the missing ProxyPass to the README + flips the workflow's HTTP-error path to ::error:: + exit 1; carkedit-api and carkedit-online ship the identical one-line workflow change. Plus an operator-side Apache config update on prod.

commits: fix: document notify ProxyPass + hard-fail merge workflow on HTTP error (carkedit-deploy#16)
ci: hard-fail notify-merge workflow on HTTP error (carkedit-api#118)
ci: hard-fail notify-merge workflow on HTTP error (carkedit-online#235)
version: bump to v0.05.0000 (post-merge MINOR) (carkedit-deploy#17)
framing: This is the natural sequel to the previous post: I'd just wired DISCORD_WEBHOOK_DEV so dev deploys would announce in #dev-updates, and Brennan asked the obvious next question — 'okay, but why isn't the channel actually getting Dev Update posts for any of the recent merges?' One curl later we had the answer: the notify endpoint at /api/admin/notify/merge had been silently 404-ing on every PR merge across three repos, and would have continued doing so indefinitely. The combination of two design choices made it invisible: (1) putting the notify endpoint at a sibling prefix to /deploy/ (intentional — keeps deploy-token scope narrow) meant Apache needed its own ProxyPass for it, which was never documented and never added; (2) the workflow's soft-fail (echo a warning, exit 0) meant every '404, never reached service' incident shows as a green run on the GitHub Actions tab. Two bugs each silent on their own, together producing the perfectly invisible outage. The fix is mostly documentation (the README now explains BOTH prefixes are required and why) plus a one-line workflow change in three repos so the next regression of this kind goes red instead of green. The broader lesson: when you have a soft-fail in CI, ask 'is this workflow's only job the thing I'm soft-failing on?' — if yes, the soft-fail is a hide-the-bug switch, not a resilience feature.

feature.name: PM2 Health Dots on Deploy Versions Table
feature.description: Each row of the Deployed Versions table on /deploy.html now carries a green/yellow/red status circle indicating PM2 process health on that environment's server. The dot rolls up the worst-case state of carkedit-deploy + carkedit-api; hovering reveals a multi-line tooltip with each app's exact state.

commits: feat: per-env PM2 health dot on deploy versions table
framing: Until now the versions table told you whether the right code was deployed, but nothing about whether it was actually RUNNING. If carkedit-api crashed under load, the green ✓ next to its version was technically truthful and totally misleading. The new dot answers the question the table was supposed to answer all along: is this env healthy right now? It pulls straight from pm2 jlist on the box, caches for 3s, and degrades gracefully when something on the path is broken — unreachable servers and older deploy services both fall back to a grey "unknown" dot so the table keeps working during rolling deploys.

feature.name: Self-Deploy Auth Token Fix
feature.description: Added .deploy-token-carkedit-deploy to the carkedit-deploy auth middleware so the self-deploy GitHub Actions workflow can authenticate. The third deploy target was introduced in PR #12 along with server-side token files and GH secrets, but the in-code allowlist (TOKEN_FILES_DEFAULT in src/auth.ts) was never widened — so every self-deploy run was hitting HTTP 401 invalid_token.

commits: fix: add .deploy-token-carkedit-deploy to TOKEN_FILES_DEFAULT
framing: Small patch (5 lines of real code), but a useful pattern reminder: a feature is not shipped until the auth layer knows about it. The self-deploy pipeline was end-to-end complete on paper — PR #12 added the deploy target and its routes, the servers had the token files, the GitHub secrets were set — but the in-code TOKEN_FILES_DEFAULT array still only listed the original two tokens. The final hop was silent until you saw 401s in every workflow run. Mostly worth blogging as a case study in cross-system rollout: when wiring up a new capability across infra + auth + code, the auth allowlist is the one that bites latest and quietest.

commits: fix: stop "Staging" label wrapping in Deployed Versions table

Fixed in a single session with the full three-gate workflow even though the diff is essentially two CSS lines — discipline scales down.

feature.name: See more button on Recent commits panel

screenshots.description: Initial Recent commits panel — 10 commits rendered, See more button visible at the bottom of the panel.

commits: feat: clickable # link before each version in Deployed Versions table

Now its one click from a version cell to the corresponding commit/tag on GitHub. The change is frontend-only and uses kind+version data the API already returns, so theres no backend cost. This kind of micro-friction removal is what makes a self-built dev tool feel like a product.

feature.name: Live/Staging/Dev Badges on Deploy Repo Commits
feature.description: The Recent Commits panel at dev.play.carkedit.com/deploy now attaches Live/Staging/Dev badges to carkedit-deploy commits — not just carkedit-online and carkedit-api. Each environment's badge appears on whichever deploy commit is actually running there.

commits: feat: badge currently-running deploy commit with Live/Staging/Dev
framing: The deploy dashboard's commit timeline already badged online and api commits with the env they're live on, but deploy commits never got the badge — the data just wasn't there. The /versions endpoint only knew the deploy SHA after a self-deploy through the service had completed (and written it to branch-state.json). Now the server resolves the actual on-disk HEAD SHA via git rev-parse once at startup (it can't change without a restart anyway — a self-deploy SIGTERMs the process). With the SHA exposed, the existing badge mapper picks it up. If all 3 envs run the same deploy commit → 1 row gets all 3 badges; if they diverge → 3 separate rows each get the env badge that's running them. Small fix, but it closes the last visibility gap on the deploy dashboard — Brennan can now see at a glance which deploy code is live on each environment.

screenshots.description: Recent commits panel with paired commits showing both online and api chips on a single row

commits: fix: pull boundary-paired commits into /commits slice
framing: Coordinated PR pairs that land within the same minute across carkedit-online and carkedit-api are now reliably visualised as a single row in the /deploy timeline, regardless of where the pair lands in the topN window. Small UX bug, but it removes a confusing class of inconsistency: the row only had to be wrong by one position to look like the change had only landed in one repo, which made the timeline subtly untrustworthy.

feature.name: See Less button on Recent commits panel
feature.description: Added a See less button next to the existing See more in the Recent commits panel of the deploy admin UI. The two share the pager row at a 70:30 width split when both are visible; when See less is hidden (at the default limit of 10) See more expands to 100% width. See less appears once the limit has been bumped above 10, decrements by one page (10), and re-hides itself at the floor.

commits: feat: add "See less" button next to "See more" (70:30 split)
fix: See more takes full width when See less is hidden
framing: Direct follow-up to the See more pagination shipped earlier the same day. See more on its own was a one-way ratchet — once you'd loaded 50 commits there was no way to collapse the panel back without a full page reload. See less closes that loop. The interesting bits are the CSS, not the JS: rather than fixed flex-basis percentages (which would have left an empty 30% gap whenever See less was hidden), the row uses grow-based ratios (flex: 7 1 0 / flex: 3 1 0). The container distributes free space by grow factor, so the 70:30 split is preserved when both children are visible and the lone visible child fills the row when the other has display:none. No JS reflow needed when buttons toggle — the layout falls out of the cascade. Also worth noting: this PR went through three rounds of merge-from-main during a 90-minute session as other branches (#34 Branches panel toggle, #35 deploy-branch highlight, #36 merge Branches panel into commits timeline, #37 Open filter, #38 scoped grey-subject fix) all landed touching the same ui.js / ui.css / ui.html. Each round resolved conflicts so the new feature coexisted with the incoming changes; 219/219 tests passed after every merge. The wider lesson: a small UX iteration shipped through a real four-gate workflow against a fast-moving main is mostly merge-management, not implementation.

feature.name: Self-Deploy Status Fix + Concurrency Guard
feature.description: Fixed a long-standing bug where every self-deploy of the carkedit-deploy webhook was silently reporting 'failed' even when the code deployed correctly (since 2026-05-15). Also added a 409 Conflict guard so a double-click on the Deploy button can't race two parallel deploys through pm2-reload.

commits: fix: persist SHA before pm2-reload + reject concurrent deploys with 409
framing: Two bugs in the deploy admin UI that masked each other. Bug A: the dashboard had been showing red 'failed' for every self-deploy since the feature shipped — the deploy actually worked, but boot-verify couldn't see the SHA because doRunDeploy only wrote it AFTER pm2-reload SIGTERMed the process. Every self-deploy was a false negative. Bug B: clicking Deploy twice quickly raced two deploys into PM2's reload lock and broke it. The fix for A made the dashboard tell the truth for the first time in 5 days; the fix for B made the dashboard's button rejection safe. The first self-deploy after merge was the first in history to correctly finalise as 'success' — caught live in production via SSH within 60 seconds of the PR merging.

feature.name: Disable Deploy buttons during active deploy
feature.description: On the /deploy dashboard, every Deploy button (the main form button plus the inline branch-Deploy chips in the Recent activity timeline) is now greyed out while a deploy is actively running. Buttons re-enable the moment the polled /status reports a terminal phase (success, failed, or skipped). Behaviour is driven by the existing status-poll loop, so a page reload mid-deploy comes up with the buttons already disabled — no flicker.

screenshots.description: Deploy dashboard during a running deploy — main and inline Deploy buttons greyed out
Deploy dashboard after the deploy succeeded — all buttons re-enabled

commits: feat: disable all Deploy buttons while a deploy is running
version: bump to v0.07.0000 (post-merge MINOR)
framing: Before this change, the only thing protecting against double-firing a deploy was a few hundred milliseconds where the main Deploy button was disabled during the POST request — and the inline per-branch Deploy chips on the commit timeline were never disabled at all. So if you clicked Deploy from the form and then noticed a different branch you wanted to push, clicking that inline chip would silently queue a second deploy on top of the first one. Subtle, easy to do, and the kind of paper cut that erodes trust in the dashboard. The fix wires every Deploy button to a single deploy-in-progress signal sourced from the same /status poll that already drives the rest of the UI — single source of truth, no new endpoints, no flicker on reload, no way to double-fire.

feature.name: Show all open branches in Recent activity
feature.description: The deploy admin's Recent activity panel now surfaces every open branch as its own row across the three deployed repos. Two server-side fixes: paginate the /branches endpoint past the 100-per-page GitHub cap, and enrich the /commits timeline with HEAD commits of branches not on main (via /commits/:sha, cached 24h by immutable SHA, concurrency-capped, with inflight de-dup). A small CSS tweak (flex-wrap: nowrap + ellipsis on the subject) keeps the rows single-line as branch chips appear.

screenshots.description: Recent activity panel with 200+ rows, each open branch rendered as its own row with a branch-name chip — including the previously-invisible dev/recent-activity-branch-label whose HEAD wasn't on main.
Full-page screenshot showing the entire enriched timeline; rows stay single-line and the subject column truncates with an ellipsis when chips would otherwise push the row to a second line.

commits: feat: show all open branches in Recent activity
fix: keep Recent activity rows on a single line with subject truncation
version: bump to v0.08.0000 (post-merge MINOR)
framing: This started with a literal user question — "why can't I see the branches with open PRs in Recent activity?" The honest answer was that the panel had never been able to: GitHub's `GET /repos/:owner/:repo/commits` only walks the default branch, so any feature-branch HEAD was invisible to the timeline, and the frontend chip-rendering logic was attaching branch chips to rows by SHA — no row, no chip. The fix turned the panel from "recent main commits with some branch labels overlaid" into "every open branch is one row, always." The constant-time-per-orphan cost is bounded by an LRU per-SHA cache (SHAs are immutable; 24h TTL is conservative). Combined with the pagination fix (carkedit-online had already silently exceeded the 100/repo cap), the deploy admin is now a complete view of in-flight work across all three repos.

feature.name: PR / MERGED tags + merge-commit row collapse

screenshots.description: Recent activity panel showing the dev/recent-activity-all-branches chip + MERGED tag folded into the (#47) merge commit row, plus a green PR tag on dev/commits-stats-rewrite

commits: feat: PR/MERGED tags + collapse merge-commit row in Recent activity
version: bump to v0.10.0000 (post-merge MINOR)
framing: Before: a merged PR whose branch wasnt yet deleted appeared as two unrelated rows in Recent activity. After: one row per PR with a clear state tag. The deploy console finally tells you at a glance which branches are still in progress vs. already on main — turning the timeline from a noisy commit log into a PR-state dashboard.

feature.name: Drop /stats/* — derive merge-embed enrichment from /commits
feature.description: Rewrote carkedit-deploy's github-stats provider to compute the Discord merge-embed's chart + 3-month commits + PRs-merged fields from /repos/.../commits and /pulls instead of GitHub's /stats/commit_activity and /stats/code_frequency endpoints. The /stats/* endpoints had been stuck at HTTP 202 for 5+ days even after upgrading to GitHub Pro — a server-side bug where the async-compute pipeline for those specific endpoints stalls on certain private repos. Drops the Lines of code field (no cheap substitute) but lights up the chart + Commits (3mo) + PRs merged that had been blank since the webhook went live.

commits: refactor: derive merge-embed stats from /commits instead of /stats/* (carkedit-deploy#43)
version: bump to v0.11.0000 (post-merge MINOR) (carkedit-deploy#50)
framing: A story about leaning on the wrong API. The Discord webhook feature had been firing for weeks, but the chart + Commits (3mo) + PRs merged + Lines of code fields had been quietly blank that entire time because they depended on GitHub's /stats/commit_activity and /stats/code_frequency endpoints. The first day of this session we burned hours assuming it was authentication: generated a fine-grained PAT, then a classic PAT, then upgraded to GitHub Pro. None of it moved the needle. The endpoints kept returning HTTP 202 indefinitely — for five days, even after the web UI's Insights pages rendered the equivalent charts fine. Turns out GitHub has a server-side bug where the async-compute pipeline for these specific endpoints permanently stalls on certain private repos. The fix wasn't more auth — it was a different data source. /commits?since=<53w> is synchronous, always returns 200, and gives us exactly what we needed once we bucket the commit dates into 52 weekly slots ourselves. ~30 minutes of code, plus 24 new tests covering pagination, week-edge behaviour, and malformed dates. The live smoke test against production returned commits3mo=889 and branchesMerged=387 — the data we'd been chasing all along. The wider lesson: GitHub's documented 'retry after a brief wait' is sometimes 'this will never resolve.' When you've waited days for a documented-async response, stop waiting and find a synchronous alternative.

framing: The versioning standard at ~/Projects/Claude Templates/rules/versioning.md has called out cross-repo version gating since v2.1.0 — but the contract was just a documented JSON field, with nothing enforcing it. This session implemented it end-to-end across two repos. The interesting design move was the deploy-side UX: rather than blocking a client deploy with an error when the api is too old, the deploy service silently chains the api deploy first. The chained api→client phases share an in-flight lock (chainedDeployInFlight) that bridges the brief gap where on-disk status reads as idle between legs, preventing racing POSTs from squeezing in. Backwards-compatible by design — historic client tags without the field deploy exactly as before. 311 / 311 carkedit-deploy tests green, 16 / 16 carkedit-online tests green, Playwright snapshot confirms the new ⚠ indicator across all three env rows. feature.name: Combined Discord deploy notifications
feature.description: When a CarkedIt release tags both carkedit-api and carkedit-online (a typical prod release), the Discord channel now receives ONE consolidated 'CarkedIt is live' embed with a row per target — instead of two separate 'CarkedIt v0.02.0006 is live' / 'CarkedIt v1.06.0187 is live' messages. The first deploy in a 15-min window POSTs the embed via the webhook ?wait=true endpoint to capture Discord's message id, and any subsequent deploys in the window PATCH that same message via the webhook /messages/{id} edit API with a combined embed listing every target seen so far.

commits: feat: combine successive deploy notifications into one edited Discord message (#71)
version: bump MM to 0.17.0000 after merging #71 (combined deploy notifications)
framing: A 'this should already work this way' UX paper-cut. Every prod release tags carkedit-api and carkedit-online near-simultaneously, and our Discord #carkedit-online channel had been getting two separate 'is live' embeds — one when the API server finished its 10-minute npm-ci/build, another when the client deploy finished a minute later. From the user's perspective it's one release but the channel told two stories. Now it's one edited message that grows in place as each target completes. The implementation choice was deliberate: a pure debounce (delay every embed by N minutes) would have made the slow-API/fast-client gap impossible to bridge without delaying every notification by ~15 minutes. Instead, post immediately for instant feedback, then use Discord's webhook PATCH /messages/{id} API to grow the same message as the rest of the release lands — best of both worlds, no notification delay, and single-target releases still render the original embed because the renderer detects the count. Architecture validation came from the wiki Hosts table: production carkedit-deploy is ONE pm2 process serving both api.carkedit.com and play.carkedit.com vhosts, so in-memory state is sufficient — no cross-process coordination needed. Per-tier ReleaseSession instances handle dev/staging/prod consistently. Self-deploys (target='deploy') deliberately bypass the session so admin events don't roll into a public release message. 19 new unit tests + 3 mock-Discord-server smoketests verified the POST→PATCH protocol locally before merge.

framing: The Promote-Build panel's whole point is one-click promotion across three repos; the old 409 rejection meant 'one click, then chase two failed GitHub Actions runs with manual rerun.' Architecturally interesting bits worth pulling out: persisted queue file (~/server/deploy-queue.json) that survives the self-deploy SIGTERM (the deploy of carkedit-deploy reloads itself via pm2, killing the running process); dedup on (target, ref) so bursty re-tagging is harmless; 16-slot cap and 15-min stale-job safety net that I haven't seen fire yet. This is PR 1 of 2 — server-side queue is in; PR 2 will convert the 9 GitHub workflows from fire-and-fail to fire-and-poll so the Actions UI shows real outcomes instead of 'request accepted'. The thing I most want readers to feel: it's worth investing in the post-merge feedback loop when the same paper cut bites twice. After the second incident I stopped working around it and shipped a real fix.

feature.name: Fix Eulogy Picker Buttons
feature.description: Phase 4 'pick eulogists' buttons were unresponsive in production, blocking the wildcard round. Fix: tightened the shared escapeHtml utility to also escape " and ' (previously only escaped <, >, &), so JSON.stringify(playerName) interpolated into onclick attributes no longer breaks the HTML parser.

screenshots.description: Phase 4 'pick eulogists' screen rendered with wildcard holder Brennan and clickable Alex / Sam chips — proves the inline onclick handlers now form valid HTML and fire selectEulogist(name) on click.

framing: A six-week-old 'fix XSS in player names' commit traded one bug for another: the JSON.stringify(name) wrapping that was supposed to harden the onclick handlers depended on escapeHtml also escaping quotes — but the textContent/innerHTML round-trip used inside escapeHtml only escapes <, >, & (because those are the only chars that *need* escaping in text content). The result: every single player name closed its onclick attribute halfway through, producing 'SyntaxError: Unexpected end of input' and dead buttons in the wildcard eulogy round. A reminder that 'safe in context A' utilities silently fail in context B, and that the next time you reach for textContent.innerHTML, write the regex chain instead.

feature.name: Players-list DEV chip + game-row expansion
feature.description: Two fixes on the admin dashboard's Players section: the per-game DEV chip now actually toggles (it was a silent no-op), and clicking a game row inside an expanded player now expands it inline with the same Settings/Players/Phases/Issues/Debug detail used by the main Games list.

commits: fix: make DEV chip clickable and add game-row expansion in Players list
fix: show DEV chip read-only in prod-preview on per-player game rows
framing:
Two complaints surfaced as one screenshot: the DEV chip in the player-expansion games list looked clickable but did nothing, and the same games list — unlike the dashboard's main Games table — never expanded a row inline.

The DEV bug was a beautiful piece of architectural irony. The component uses two delegated-event attributes: data-ps-action says 'fire this action when this element is clicked', and data-ps-stop says 'don't let clicks here bubble up to a parent action' (so empty padding inside the games subsection doesn't accidentally collapse the player). The root click handler checked data-ps-stop *first* — meaning the wrapper around the games block silently swallowed every click inside it, including clicks on the DEV button that lived inside that wrapper and carried its own data-ps-action='toggle-game-dev'. The button's CSS had an is-on state, the JSX had the right attributes, the patch endpoint was wired — the click just never reached the dispatcher. The fix isn't to remove the stop wrapper (the player-collapse invariant matters); it's to walk from the click target up to the nearest action element and only honour a stop *if it sits on that walk*. Same intent, correct ordering. It's a five-line change with a unit test that hammers six interesting click positions (player name, header-in-stop, padding-in-stop, game row, DEV button, nested stop descendant) — all six now route correctly.

The expansion side reused the dashboard's existing detail view by passing renderGameDetail and a fetchGameDetail closure as opts to mountPlayerStats. The detail HTML references window.dash.previewCard(...) for the mini-card click-throughs, and those globals already exist on the dashboard page — so injecting a function reference rather than extracting a shared module worked unchanged. Cache is shared too: open a game from the main Games list, then open the same game from inside a player, and the second open is instant. admin-users.html mounts the same component without injecting those callbacks, so it gracefully degrades back to the simple one-line summary it had before.

The takeaway is small but real: delegated-event handlers carry an implicit precedence between 'is this an action?' and 'is this in a stop region?', and the wrong order silently disables buttons rather than failing loudly. Better to ask 'where is the action?' first, then ask 'was anything in the way?'

feature.name: Branch banner without PHP, with working Switch-to-main
feature.description: Dropped the dead branch-info.php endpoint and switched the site-wide light-blue branch banner to the carkedit-deploy /api/admin/deploy/versions JSON endpoint. Banner correctly appears on dev when a non-main branch is deployed, stays hidden on staging (tag deploys) and prod. Made the banner's "Switch to main" link actually switch — one click after sign-in resets api + client + deploy to main by seeding the carkedit-deploy fragment's existing reset-to-main chain via sessionStorage.

screenshots.description: Light-blue branch banner across the top of the home page on dev — branch name + client/api versions + short SHA + Switch-to-main button. This is the proof the new /api/admin/deploy/versions wiring renders the banner correctly with no PHP in the loop.
Same banner on /stats.html — confirms the script renders on every page that includes branch-banner.js, not just the home page.

commits: fix: drop PHP from branch banner — use /api/admin/deploy/versions
feat: auto-trigger deploy when arriving via banner Switch-to-main
fix: banner Switch-to-main resets api + client + deploy, not just client
framing: The real story is the rediscovery arc, not the code. Three sessions ago I shipped PR #241 to fix the same broken banner — by teaching branch-info.php to handle detached HEAD from carkedit-deploy's git-reset-hard pattern and the new branch-state.json schema. That fix worked. The bug came back anyway, because between then and now PHP execution itself was disabled on dev and prod (only staging still runs it). The banner's fetch("branch-info.php").json() returned the raw .php source, silently threw, and the banner never rendered. So the actual fix this round was to stop depending on PHP at all — the carkedit-deploy service has been quietly exposing /api/admin/deploy/versions for weeks with everything the banner needs (envTier, deployed ref.kind/value/sha, version). That's also where the second arc kicked in. The naive fix made the banner's "Switch to main" do a single client-only deploy. The user clicked it, watched only the client come back to main, and surfaced a screenshot showing the api row still pinned to dev/discord-notifications with a red ✗. Rather than reinvent the chain logic in deploy.html, I noticed carkedit-deploy's fragment already has a Reset-to-main button that walks api → client → deploy via sessionStorage["cd-reset-chain"], persists across the page reloads each deploy triggers, and picks the right ref per env tier (branch=main on dev, latest staging tag on staging, latest release tag on prod). So the host page now just seeds that sessionStorage key when it arrives at deploy.html?reset=main&auto=1 and lets the existing fragment do its thing. Two-line behavioural change, zero new sequencing code. Broader lesson: when a fix relies on a server-side dependency (PHP, in this case), assume the dependency can disappear under you, and prefer wiring through the service you're already running — even if the path is longer.

feature.name: Discord notifications for game + account lifecycle
feature.description: Posts a Discord embed when a non-dev online game starts (the moment the room leaves lobby), when a non-dev game finishes (online via Colyseus, or local single-device via POST /api/carkedit/games), or when a new user account is created. Single env var DISCORD_APP_WEBHOOK_URL per box; dev + staging share the existing 'CarkedIt Online - DevAPP' webhook, prod gets its own new one. Fire-and-forget HTTP with a 5s abort, never-throws, missing-URL short-circuits — a Discord outage can never block a game starting, completing, or a user signing in.

The phase transitioned from lobby → die_phase, which is the exact code point that fires the 'Game started' notify hook. Server v0.02.0010 home page on http://localhost:4510 — the local dev server used for Gate 2 verification. Server-version footer confirms the binary running has my changes.

commits: feat: Discord webhook notifications for game + account lifecycle (#127)
framing: The shipped code was straightforward — a 195-line webhook poster with 11 unit tests, a few hook points in GameRoom and users.ts, an env var, done. The interesting part was what happened *after* Gate 3 was queued for approval: the user deployed the branch to dev and reported 'no notification in Discord.' That's where the feature actually became a feature. SSH'd to the dev box and found the carkedit-api process couldn't see DISCORD_APP_WEBHOOK_URL — the variable they thought they'd set was in `/home/bitnami/server/.env-carkedit-deploy`, which is the env file the *deploy* service reads. carkedit-api reads `/home/bitnami/server/carkedit-api/.env`, which had no Discord var at all. Two services on the same box, two env files, easy to conflate. Fix was 60 seconds: copy DISCORD_WEBHOOK_DEV's value into the api env file, `pm2 restart --update-env`. Verified with two synthetic POST /games calls that landed real embeds in #dev-updates. Then applied the same fix to staging (same dev URL) and prod (the new prod webhook the user supplied), so as soon as the merge propagates to those tiers, they'll start posting. The wiki update is the real artifact of this session — a clear 'these are different env files, do not confuse' warning in the page intro plus a full per-tier setup table, so the next person doesn't repeat the discovery. Net for users: real-time visibility into actual game activity vs. deploy noise. Net for the project: two semantically-distinct flows now have one wiki page that explains both.

feature.name: Skip npm-ci when package-lock.json is unchanged
feature.description: The carkedit-deploy service now hashes the post-reset package-lock.json before each deploy and compares it to a new optional lockfileSha field on BranchEntry. When the lockfile is unchanged since the last successful deploy of that target, npm-ci is short-circuited via a synthetic step record (no subprocess spawn) — saving 1-3 minutes per api/deploy push on the common case. ?force=true bypasses the skip.

screenshots.description: Live carkedit-deploy /health endpoint responding while the new lockfile-hash skip path is integration-tested on localhost:4509 — the same scratch service that proved the skip works end-to-end (matching hash → 0ms synthetic record; force=true → 338ms real spawn; hash mismatch → 321ms real spawn).

commits: feat: skip npm-ci when package-lock.json is unchanged (#75)
version: bump MM to 0.20.0000 after merging #75 (npm-ci lockfile-hash skip)
framing: Deploys were dominated by a single slow step — npm ci — that wiped and re-fetched a 344MB node_modules tree on every push, even when no dependency had actually changed. This is the kind of friction that compounds: every Gate 3 merge, every promote-build burst, every emergency hotfix paid the same 1-3 minute toll. The fix mirrors the existing SHA-unchanged short-circuit pattern, scoped one level finer (lockfile content vs. commit SHA), so the data path and skipped-step semantics felt familiar to anyone who already knew the deploy service. Future deploys for backend code-only changes will start to feel snappy.
